title: Revalidation
summary: Refresh only the route data that needs to change.

sections.title: Automatic refresh
sections.body: Successful actions refresh the active page, previously loaded fetchers, and registered root/layout data. A fetcher loader read does not trigger revalidation. Each route can opt out with shouldRevalidate.

sections.title: Control refresh
sections.body: shouldRevalidate receives currentUrl, nextUrl, url, reason, defaultShouldRevalidate, and mutation context when available. Returning false skips a refresh. The function must be synchronous.

sections.title: Manual refresh
sections.body: useRevalidator returns a function, not an object with state and revalidate fields. Manual refresh also respects shouldRevalidate.
sections.code:
const revalidate = useRevalidator();

<button onClick={() => void revalidate()}>Refresh</button>

sections.title: Target a route
sections.body: Pass a route ID or its registered path pattern. An array selects multiple routes. Only active page data, loaded fetchers, and registered layouts matching that target refresh; this does not navigate or load an inactive page. For /items/:id, use that pattern rather than /items/42. Unknown targets do nothing. shouldRevalidate still applies.

sections.title: Root and layout data
sections.body: The Preact root integration registers its root under root by default, or RootModule.id when provided. Set loaderPath to a registered data route when the root needs refreshing. Custom React or Preact layouts can register their own callback on the router and unregister it during cleanup. No endpoint name is assumed.

sections.title: Avoid stale UI
sections.body: Opting out means you own the freshness decision. Keep the default true until you can identify no-op actions or URL changes that leave the active loader result valid.
